Let me parse this certificate.

Certificate number: R60/2000-A-NL1-22.17 revision 0
Scheme: A
Project number: 2611823
Page total: 3
Member state: The Netherlands
Date issued: 10 June 2022 → 2022-06-10
OIML issuer ID: NL1

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V.
- Address lines: Thijsseweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, The Netherlands (note OCR says "Thijssseweg" — likely Thijsseweg, but I should keep as-is? "Thijssseweg 11" — I'll keep as in source, maybe correct to "Thijsseweg 11"? Rule says don't fabricate; keep as-is "Thijssseweg 11".)
- Person responsible: M.Ph.D. Schmidt
- Phone: +31 88 6362332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- oiml_issuer_id: NL1

Applicants:
- Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd., 22 ZhengQiang Road, ChangZhou, JiangSu, 213125, P.R.China

Manufacturers: same (applicant and manufacturer together). The cert says "Applicant and Manufacturer" — so I'll add both applicant and manufacturer entries.

Certified type:
- Category: "Load cell"
- Type designations: GDD, SLC720
- Module designation: The characterization says "Digital load cell". Hmm — for load cell certs, module_designation is "Analog load cell" | "Digital load cell"? The schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null but the table says "Digital load cell". I'll use "Digital load cell".
- Description: "A compression load cell, with strain gauges, equipped with electronics. Registered trade name: Mettler-Toledo"

Model family: Emax range "15 t up to and including 50 t". This is a range, not discrete models. So no model family needed? Actually it's a continuous range of capacities. The characteristics table has single values, not comma-separated lists. So model_level not needed. Emax = {min: 15, max: 50}, unit "t". Should I create models? No — it's a range, treat as type_level.

Characteristics type_level:
- characterization_of_load_cell_capabilities: "Digital load cell" — could be part of module_designation instead. I'll put module_designation: "Digital load cell".
- maximum_capacity (emax): {min: 15, max: 50}, unit "t"
- minimum_dead_load: 50, unit "kg"
- accuracy_class: "C" (string value; unit null)
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 5000, footnote_markers ["1)"] — actually the footnote marker (1) applies. Footnotes are: "1. The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately." So footnote marker "1)" on n, Y, Z.
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 11900, footnote ["1)"]
- ratio_z_emax_over_dr: 5000 — formula Z = Emax/(2*DR); value 5000, footnote ["1)"]
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C"
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.8 (note 0,8 → 0.8), unit null
- humidity_class: "CH"
- safe_overload: 200, unit "%"; reference "Emax" — I could add safe_overload_reference: "Emax" per rule 3's example. Let me include: safe_overload: {value: 200, unit_symbol: "%"}, safe_overload_reference: {value: "Emax"}.
- recommended_excitation: {min: 12, max: 24}, unit "V", plus power supply type DC? It's excitation DC. I could add recommended_excitation_type: "DC". Let me split: recommended_excitation_voltage: {min 12, max 24, V}, recommended_excitation_type: "DC". Actually simpler: recommended_excitation {value: {min:12, max:24}, unit_symbol: "V"} and separate "recommended_excitation_type": {"value": "DC"}. Hmm, the schema example splits power supply voltage/frequency/type. I'll do voltage + type.
- excitation_maximum: 24, unit "V", type DC → excitation_maximum: {value:24, unit:"V"}; maybe excitation_maximum_type: "DC". I'll include type field.
- transducer_material: "Stainless steel"
- atmospheric_protection: "Hermetically welded"
- electromagnetic_environment_class: "E2"
- number_of_counts_for_emax: "Y * 5 / pLC" — formula, keep as string "Y * 5 / p_LC" — avoid subscript LaTeX; plain "Y * 5 / pLC". Use "Y*5/pLC".
- software_identification: "Version number: 1.xx" with footnote (2). Value as string "1.xx", footnote_markers ["2)"].

Footnotes:
- "1)" : "The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately."
- "2)" : "xx is a number between 00 and 99 representing updates of the non legally relevant part of the software."

Recommendation: id "R60", edition 2000, amendment null, scheme "A", accuracy_classes ["C"].

Test reports:
- NMi-10201060-01, dated 4 December 2012, pages 69, role "type_evaluation_report"? They are OIML Test Reports. role: "test_report"? The schema roles: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. OIML Test Report — I'll use "test_report" for both. Date: 2012-12-04 and 2022-05-13.
- NMi-2611823-01, 2022-05-13, 23 pages.

Revision history:
- revision "0", date "2022-06-10", changes "Initial issue. Replaces previous MAA certificate(s) for this load cell type".

Additional: certificate.number: "R60/2000-A-NL1-22.17", revision: 0 → revision_history covers it. The certificate schema doesn't have a revision field except revision_history. Number string includes revision 0 — I'll keep number as "R60/2000-A-NL1-22.17".

Date issued: 10 June 2022 → "2022-06-10".

Also the US additional requirements — could be captured? Not in schema explicitly. Could add to description or omit. I'll omit or add maybe as a note. Schema doesn't have a field; rule 8 says don't fabricate. I could skip.

No matrix tables needed.

Output JSON.
